subject: Intermittent high tail latency & 502s — suspected DNS / firewall handshake delay
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@edgesupply.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@edgesupply.com
Date: Mon, 27 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden spike in tail latency + 502s across model inference

Hi Sofia,

We're seeing a spike in tail latency for API calls from our EU storefront over the last 90 minutes — 95th/99th p50 -> p99 latency jumped and ~3% 502s and a few customer reports of failed checkouts. Traces point to long TCP/TLS handshakes and intermittent 502 responses from the Redwood edge. Attaching a short latency graph (PNG).

We haven't changed our client or traffic patterns. Can you confirm if there are any known infra changes, regional peering adjustments, or firewall rules that might cause delayed handshakes? This is impacting conversion already and needs a fast path to mitigation.

Thanks,
Liam
SRE Lead — EdgeSupply

Attachment: edgesupply_latency_summary.png (image/png, 240KB)
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and the graph, that helps. I'm escalating to our SRE immediately and looping in Sales/CS so they have visibility.

— Sofia
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, Liam O'Connor <liam@edgesupply.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden spike in tail latency + 502s across model inference

Looking at initial telemetry: I pulled the flow logs and backend health — no bulk model node CPU/GPUs are saturated. However, flow logs show a subset of client IPs experiencing 200–600ms additional handshake time between our edge and the customer origin-facing NAT. Two things to chase immediately: DNS resolution delays to our edge-service FQDN from the customer's POP, and a firewall/proxy silently re-negotiating TLS (we've seen some middleboxes introduce a full handshake).

Planned next steps (immediate):
1) If you can provide a pcap (short capture) and an example request-id, we'll correlate with our side.
2) We'll temporarily route that customer's traffic to a nearby redundant edge POP (route-level mitigation) and keep TTL low so we can revert quickly.
3) We'll open an INF-1248 ticket to track root cause and rollback actions.

Hypothesis: split-horizon DNS or an upstream proxy change caused the client to hit a path that inserts an opaque proxy/firewall doing TLS interception, adding handshake latency and occasionally dropping streams, producing 502s.

Marcus
Sr. SRE — Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 28 Mar 2028 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Mitigation in place + next steps (INF-1248)

Liam — temporary routing to a redundant POP was applied at 15:18 PDT and we observed a drop in tail handshake times and 502 rate returned to baseline within 4 minutes. We correlated your pcap (req-20280327-5542) and see the pattern Marcus mentioned: an extra TLS negotiation occurring after initial SYN/ACK consistent with a middlebox re-negotiation.

Next steps:
- INF-1248 created to track root cause and follow-up: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1248
- We'll maintain the temporary route for 24 hours while we work with your colo and our peering partners to identify the specific device/config that caused the handshake insertion.
- We'll provide a short post-mortem within 72 hours and an interim credits proposal if the impact is confirmed to be on our routing decisions (TBD based on root cause).

Please let us know if you want us to pivot to a more aggressive fix (permanent route change for your account) while investigations complete — we will consult with product/ops for implications.

Thanks for the detailed traces — that helped surface the middlebox behavior quickly.

Marcus Lin
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
